fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV honestly presents a mechanical engineer transitioning into data engineering, not an established senior data-platform engineer. Python reporting automation, SQL querying and specification-based validation are useful transferable evidence, but do not establish platform operations, cloud, advanced SQL, data modelling or governance expertise. The letter acknowledges development needs broadly, without directly confronting the substantial seniority and production-platform gap. Stack items are treated as role expectations, although the ad does not separately demand prior experience in every named tool.

artefacts: Both employment date ranges appear twice in the PDF: once right-aligned beside the job heading and again in the italic employer-description line.
issues: The PDF differs from the checked CV text through duplicated employment dates; the tool flagged this but the final PDF retains the duplication.
The skills list gives substantial space to mechanical tools instead of separating relevant data skills from additional engineering skills.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: data quality (test-data checks against specifications, not platform-wide governance)
reasons: Text extraction is orderly, headings are conventional and contact information is intact.
Python and SQL are supported by concrete work examples, but most core platform and cloud terms are absent.
The headline and employment history identify a mechanical/test engineer, with no production data-platform role.
The missing stack keywords mostly reflect real evidence gaps and should not be added as claimed skills.

issues: “Across 12 years ... I have used Python and SQL” can imply a longer history with these tools than the source establishes.
It explains a career transition but does not provide a convincing case for senior platform ownership or directly address the lack of production cloud/platform experience.
The closing values paragraph is somewhat generic despite correctly naming the company's values.
strengths: Names Halden Pay and the exact target role.
Connects the application to reusable shared platform capabilities.
Uses the strongest relevant example: Python validation/report automation with a supported time-saving metric.
Accurately presents SQL Server trend analysis and avoids fabricating cloud or orchestration experience.
Uses Together, Ownership and Pace consistently with the supplied company information.

spacing_issues: The CV has a relatively large gap between the contact line and PROFILE.
The letter's LinkedIn URL wraps onto its own header line; this is readable but less tidy than a deliberately structured two-line contact block.
consistency_issues: Employment dates are repeated in both role headings and descriptive sublines in the CV.
The CV uses a centred large header and blue section rules; the letter uses a smaller left-aligned header and blue contact links. They share a serif typeface but are not fully coordinated.
issues: The images and measurements show adequate margins, readable 11-point body text and no clipping or overlap.
The cover letter's lower-page whitespace is normal for a one-page letter, not an unnecessary extra page.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “Across 12 years in mechanical engineering, I have used Python and SQL” is temporally imprecise; “In my current engineering role, I use Python and SQL” would avoid implying 12 years of tool experience.
“Uses Python ... Experienced querying ... Interested in moving” mixes third-person and fragment-style profile phrasing; consistent noun-led or first-person-free phrasing would read more smoothly.

evaluation.summary: The documents are readable, professional and largely faithful to the candidate's material, retaining the strongest Python automation and SQL evidence without inventing a cloud-platform background. The letter is genuinely tailored to Halden Pay's role and values, although its opening slightly stretches the apparent duration of Python and SQL experience. The central limitation is real fit: the material does not establish senior production-platform ownership, cloud engineering, advanced SQL or data modelling, so screening prospects are low. The CV PDF also repeats employment dates, a visible generation defect that remains despite the tool's warning.
